findings.title: Specialist validation is bypassed by provenance rewriting
findings.reason: The attach helper overwrites all scope/provenance fields and recomputes the identity before the caller validates the entry. A multi-symbol, wrong-symbol, or wrong-direction candidate can be relabeled as the current island and accepted.
findings.recommendation: Validate existing scope and provenance before attaching; reject conflicting non-empty metadata and only add fields to an unprovenanced candidate when that is explicitly allowed.

findings.title: Standalone RB cannot resume specialist Phase 2 pools
findings.reason: The specialist writer includes symbols in the resume identity, but _load_phase2_outputs omits them. The run_phase(3/4) caller consequently reports an identity mismatch and sends empty pools to RB.
findings.recommendation: Derive and pass the current symbol set when loading specialist identities, and validate resumed specialist entries before handing them to RB.

findings.title: Per-island cache artifacts are collision-prone and survive forced regeneration
findings.reason: Filename sanitization is not injective, and per-island files have no data/resume identity. The normal generator loads old island pools using only feature/schema checks. Base Phase 2 cleanup does not remove these files, so old or another-symbol chromosomes can seed a new island.
findings.recommendation: Use collision-free symbol tokens, write per-island input identities, clear or validate island artifacts on force, and run single-symbol provenance validation on every resumed entry.

findings.title: RB engine copies drop nested Phase 2 provenance
findings.reason: _rule_to_engine does not copy rule['provenance']; the helper is used for capital-budget normalization and final strategy rules. The resulting RB rules_set cannot retain the attached provenance record.
findings.recommendation: Copy the provenance record read-only through every RB rule transformation and add an assertion covering carried['provenance'].

findings.title: Configuration audit records raw rather than resolved mode
findings.reason: validate_config accepts surrounding whitespace and case, and runtime routing normalizes it, but effective_config_snapshot writes the raw value. This makes the config audit disagree with the resolved run manifest.
findings.recommendation: Use resolve_phase2_symbol_mode() in the audit snapshot.

findings.title: Production-mode tests bypass the specialist implementation
findings.reason: The routing/persistence test replaces generate_specialist_pools with a lambda, and the provenance test calls the validator directly. These tests cannot expose cache reuse, default Rule_Pool_Generator behavior, loader identity mismatch, or nested RB provenance loss.
findings.recommendation: Add a production-path test for default specialist generation/resume and a standalone Phase 3/4 RB handoff assertion.

notes: Static review found blocking correctness and integration failures. git diff --check passed. The required pytest command was independently attempted but denied by shell policy, so runtime verification is CANNOT_VERIFY; package/implementer test claims were not used as proof.
